trickyParts: Nothing guarantees Envoy's factory runs before Legion's, so every consumer resolves the interface lazily (envoyPluginInterface() get-or-create) and publishEnvoyPluginInterface at another version warns once and does not join (first wins), which keeps this repository's own dev checkout usable where two Envoy copies load at different interface versions.

The interface holds process-wide state only (instances array, managedSessions, regained slot, the injected-turns map, the bootstrapped-session holder); Oh My Pi re-binds every extension factory per in-process task subagent, so a per-instance function slot would be overwritten (docs/solutions/envoy/heartbeat-role-reassertion-and-regain-hooks.md). A publisher is recorded once however many times it re-binds.

The Go gate judges not loaded → legacy loaded → Envoy absent → Envoy mismatch → Envoy loaded-from → prompt names, so an operator without pi-envoy reads 'install @sjawhar/pi-envoy', never 'finds no skill dispatch'; the pod lane passes both roots as explicit extensions (Envoy first) and the probe reads LEGION_PROMPT_ROOTS.

This pod's Oh My Pi (18.6.0) differed from the base commit's .omp-pin (18.2.9); the pinned 18.2.9 build was fetched from the public release to run the real-binary suites before the merge, and after main (whose pin is 18.6.0) was merged forward the proofs were re-run on the pod's binary, which is that pin.
